checks.description: Win32 selects the custom focus path by default rather than the system ring.
The custom ring is visible only while the root is focused with keyboard modality.
Programmatic focus uses the last root modality.
Disabled and noninteractive targets never show custom focus feedback.
Detaching or disabling a native focus target invalidates pending focus requests.
alwaysVisible selects the custom path and bypasses modality only while focused; useSystemFocusRing remains an explicit composition override.
Custom rings remain mounted across focus/blur and do not intercept input.
Internal focus-target refs compose with caller refs on the actual interactive root rather than a structural or descendant target.
Object/callback refs, cleanup, ref replacement, and unmount/remount retain exactly one live focus target.
Native self-focus is distinguished from bubbled descendant focus events.
Changing root modality updates an already-focused custom ring without requiring blur/refocus or scene-wide rerenders.
The actual focus owner uses either the native ring or the custom slot, never competing rings.
ThemedRoot supplies root modality, with nested theme boundaries sharing the controller and independent scenes retaining separate modality.
Custom ring geometry and shared theme colors remain correct under high contrast, display scaling, clipping, and active/inactive native windows.
The custom dual ring surrounds the whole row with the shared colors, widths, and resolved component radius.

limitations: This is a premade reviewed checklist derived from SPEC requirements and companions, not an automatically generated or exhaustive maturity policy.
Empty tests arrays mean no approved mapping for that check, not necessarily that no test exists.
Only the existing named native Checkbox callback is mapped; passing it covers binary native clicks and native role, not all state or accessibility behavior.
Shared check IDs repeat identical definitions under multiple requirements; all linked tests must qualify before the check passes.
The macOS focus case and non-Win32 platform tables remain recorded without Win32 requirement credit.
